question: Why are locking and safety devices important on a combination vehicle?
choice_a: They have no function related to coupling
choice_b: The trailer could uncouple during travel if the locking mechanisms are not secured
choice_c: They only affect ride comfort
choice_d: They are purely cosmetic hardware
explanation: The manual explains that the trailer could uncouple during travel if the locking mechanisms are not secured, and safety devices help keep the locking mechanism in place and provide assistance should the connection fail.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Locking and Safety Devices

question: For all other (non-fifth-wheel) coupling systems, what must be inspected regarding the locking mechanism or latch?
choice_a: That it can be opened with one hand while driving
choice_b: That it is replaced after every trip
choice_c: That it is painted a distinct color from the frame
choice_d: That it has no missing or broken parts and the pintle or hitch release lever or latch is locked in place and secure
explanation: The manual requires inspecting the locking mechanism or latch for missing or broken parts and making sure the pintle or hitch release lever or latch is locked in place and secure.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.1 Locking and Safety Devices, All Other Coupling Systems

question: What must be true of the landing gear before travel?
choice_a: It must be removed entirely
choice_b: It must remain partially lowered for stability
choice_c: It must be fully raised, with no missing parts, a secure crank handle, and undamaged support frame and landing pads
choice_d: It must be lubricated with brake fluid
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the landing gear is fully raised, has no missing parts, the crank handle is secure, and the support frame and landing pads are not damaged.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only, Landing Gear & Clearance

question: On a tractor semi-trailer, what must be inspected regarding the fifth wheel and landing gear during turns?
choice_a: That the landing gear is painted a bright color for visibility during turns
choice_b: That the fifth wheel is positioned properly so the tractor frame will clear the landing gear during turns
choice_c: That the fifth wheel is disconnected before any turn
choice_d: That the landing gear touches the ground during all turns
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that the fifth wheel is positioned properly so that the tractor frame will clear the landing gear during turns (fixed or sliding fifth wheel), for tractor semi-trailers.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only, Landing Gear & Clearance

question: Where must reflective tape be inspected on a trailer?
choice_a: On the sides and rear of the trailer, checking that it is present and affixed securely
choice_b: Only on the front bumper
choice_c: Only on the landing gear
choice_d: Only on the roof
explanation: The manual requires inspecting that reflector tape on the sides and rear of the trailer are present and affixed securely to the vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only, Reflective Tape

question: According to the manual, for which vehicle type is reflective tape only required?
choice_a: All power units
choice_b: Passenger buses
choice_c: Straight trucks
choice_d: Trailers (though some jurisdictional laws may also require it for school buses)
explanation: The manual states reflective tape is only required for trailers, and some jurisdictional laws may require reflective tape for school buses.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, 11.6.2 Trailers Only, Reflective Tape

question: What must happen before you can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: There is no prerequisite; tests may be taken in any order
choice_b: You must complete a written exam
choice_c: You must pass the Vehicle Inspection test
choice_d: You must pass the on-road driving test
explanation: The manual states the Vehicle Inspection test must be passed before you can proceed to the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Basic Control Skills Test transition note

question: On the CDL Vehicle Inspection checklists, which checklist item is marked with an asterisk (*) for automatic failure if not performed correctly?
choice_a: The lug nuts check
choice_b: The horn check
choice_c: The air or hydraulic brake check
choice_d: The reflective tape check
explanation: The checklists mark the air or hydraulic brake check with an asterisk noting "Automatic failure if not performed correctly."
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Class A/B/C Checklists

question: Which items appear on the Class A (combination vehicle) checklist that do NOT appear on the Class B or C straight vehicle checklist?
choice_a: Combination-vehicle-only items such as air/electric lines, fifth wheel/pintle hook/tow hitch, kingpin/apron/gap, landing gear, and reflective tape
choice_b: The service brake check
choice_c: Lug nuts and tires
choice_d: Windshield and traffic monitoring devices
explanation: The Class A checklist for tractor semi-trailer, truck & trailer, or bus & trailer includes a "Combination Vehicles Only" section (air & electric lines & connectors, fifth wheel skid plate or pintle hook or tow hitch, kingpin & apron & gap, locking & safety devices) and a "Trailer Only" section (landing gear & clearance, reflective tape) that do not appear on the Class B or C straight vehicle checklist.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 11 - Vehicle Inspection, Class A Checklist vs. Class B or C Checklist
